text:
sam_support: FYI customer on Dedicated hit a CI break after bumping the Go SDK to a v2 tagged release. `go get` fails with 401 from the proxy and a module path parse error. They rolled back to v1 and CI passed.

raj_oncall: can you paste the customer's go.mod and the `go get`/CI output?

sam_support: sure — sending clipped bits below. they also mentioned they use a `replace` to a local path in their monorepo.

sam_support: ```
module github.com/customer/project

require (
    github.com/redwood/inference-go v2.1.0
)

// local dev override present in their repo
replace github.com/redwood/inference-go => ../inference-go
```

sam_support: CI log: ```
go: github.com/redwood/inference-go@v2.1.0: parsing go.mod:
	module declares its path as: github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2
		but was required as: github.com/redwood/inference-go
get "https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/redwood/inference-go/@v/v2.1.0.mod": 401 Unauthorized
```

lin_devex: two things jumping out: 1) module path vs import path mismatch — v2 modules must use `/v2` in the module path, and 2) `replace` to a local path with the wrong module path will make `go` try to fetch the tagged v2 from the proxy. If `GOPRIVATE` isn't set, it'll hit the proxy and fail with 401 for private repos.

raj_oncall: do we have a known support KB for customers upgrading to our v2 SDK? Might need a quick note about `module` path and `replace` caveats.

tom_eng: I'll take this. sounds like the SDK released v2 tag but the module's `module` line already had `/v2` (correct). Customers who used `replace` pointing at local v1-style checkout or who didn't update import paths will hit that parsing error. The 401 is because CI env doesn't set `GOPRIVATE` or auth to the git host.

tom_eng: short remediation steps for the customer: 
1) If using a local `replace`, update the replaced module path to the v2 module path: `replace github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2 => ../inference-go` and ensure the local checkout's `go.mod` has `module github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2`.
2) Ensure CI has GOPRIVATE or appropriate auth: `export GOPRIVATE=github.com/redwood/*` and a token for private repo access so it doesn't use proxy.golang.org.
3) As a quick workaround remove the `replace` and use the v2 tag in `require` if possible.

sam_support: I sent those to the customer; they confirmed updating GOPRIVATE fixed the 401 in their CI but then hit import path mismatches locally.

lin_devex: we should add a short checklist to docs/quickstart and devx migration guide: "Upgrading to go SDK v2" covering module path, replace, CI env vars. Also add a quick grep script to detect bad `replace` usage in customer repos during support triage.

tom_eng: agreed. I'll open a PR in the SDK repo to add a release-note snippet and a CI job that validates that tags and module paths are consistent (e.g., `go list -m all` on a v2 tag).

ci-bot: created issue INFR-3421: "go SDK v2: add release validation and migration docs" and attached logs.

sam_support: thanks all — I'll mark this thread as customer-impacting until docs/PR land. keeping customer updated. :thumbsup:
